requirement:
TOML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a value on the same line. A `#` inside a quoted
string belongs to the string.
rationale:
One test covers `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.attachments`: `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. Its `test.toml` case uses the source `# first\n# second\na = '# literal' # real\n"# key" = """# literal"""\n`. It asserts the exact, ordered list of every attachment the outline reports, with kind and span text: `(Comment, "# first")`, `(Comment, "# second")` and `(Comment, "# real")`.

Mapping obligations to assertions:
- **Only `Comment` attachments.** The assertion compares the whole list of `(kind, text)` pairs. Any non-Comment attachment or extra attachment would fail it.
- **Each `#` comment is one attachment.** `# first` and `# second` are adjacent lines, and each is expected as its own entry. They are not merged into one attachment.
- **A trailing comment after a value on the same line is an attachment.** `a = '# literal' # real` must yield `# real`.
- **A `#` inside a quoted string belongs to the string.** Three strings are tested: the single-quoted literal `'# literal'` on the value side, the double-quoted key `"# key"`, and the triple-quoted multi-line string `"""# literal"""`. None of them may produce an attachment, and the exact-equality assertion enforces that.

Other `#`-in-string forms, such as a plain `"..."` value or `'''` strings, fall into the same input class as the cases above. The text does not name any further boundaries. The test is marked with `{test}` for this requirement, so there is no marking gap.
